name: George Bush Intercontinental Airport
before:
Houston's main international airport, about 23 miles north of downtown, and one of United Airlines' largest hubs. It is second in Texas for international passengers behind Dallas Fort Worth and fifteenth busiest in the United States overall.

It is big and spread out: five terminals and 10,000 acres with five runways. Two people movers hold it together. The Skyway runs airside between all five terminals, so a connecting passenger stays inside security. The Subway runs landside between the terminals and the airport hotel.

Terminals D and E have the international arrivals facility, and Terminal D has gates built for the A380 and 747-8. Terminal A takes non-United domestic carriers across two concourses and 21 gates, and Terminal B is used for United Express.

It opened in 1969 as Houston Intercontinental and was renamed in 1997 after George H. W. Bush, the forty first president and a Houston resident. Before United, it was a hub for Continental and, earlier, Eastern and Texas International.
after:
Houston's main international airport, about 23 miles north of downtown. It is a hub for United Airlines and, with more than 48 million passengers in 2025, the fifteenth busiest airport in the United States. For international passengers it is second in Texas, behind Dallas Fort Worth.

It is big and spread out: five terminals, five runways and 10,000 acres. The Skyway runs airside between all five terminals, so a connecting passenger stays inside security, while the Subway runs landside between the terminals and the airport hotel.

Most international flights use Terminals D and E, with customs in the Terminal E arrivals hall. Terminal A is mainly for other airlines' domestic flights and Terminal B for United Express. United is rebuilding Terminal B, with a new 22-gate North Concourse due to open in autumn 2026.

It opened in 1969 as Houston Intercontinental and was later renamed after President George HW Bush.
